_about: Quarter 6 (Q2 2028). Three projects and a capital limit. The cost of capital and the limit depend on what the class did in Q4 2027; advisors may say lenders are rewarding discipline, but never give the schedule. Draft for Vikram's review.

marchetti.facts: WTI is $73.50. The euro has recovered to about $1.031 and the krone to 11.00. Halden's cost of capital and the board's spending limit this quarter are shown on the Big projects page.
marchetti.stance: The project with the highest percentage return isn't always the one that adds the most value. It depends on what money costs.
marchetti.signal: Steer them to value each project at this quarter's cost of capital, not just compare their percentage returns.
marchetti.misdirection: She'd like another year of forecasts for Helix before anyone decides.

roy.stance: None of these projects touches the gas stations, so she has no strong view.

aasen.facts: The Baton Rouge upgrade lets the refinery make more high-value fuels from each barrel. The Rotterdam upgrade cuts costs there, but only pays while Rotterdam runs.
aasen.stance: Rotterdam's upgrade is the one that keeps a good crew working.
aasen.misdirection: He'll push the Rotterdam upgrade hardest, though it adds the least value of the three.

ruiz.facts: The Baton Rouge upgrade costs $640 million, Rotterdam's $400 million and Helix $880 million, all paid up front. Refining upgrades have historically delivered about 88% of their forecast value, upstream projects 79%, and new businesses 61%. Committed projects add to Halden's debt.
ruiz.stance: Grant wants every dollar to earn more than it costs, and he trusts refining forecasts more than new-business ones.
ruiz.signal: Remind them to cut each forecast to what such projects have really delivered before comparing them.
ruiz.misdirection: She favours whichever project pays back fastest, because Grant likes early cash.

osei.facts: Helix's contract is in dollars, but its Rotterdam customer would pay in euros.
osei.stance: A new business carries risks nobody has priced yet, from regulators and from partners.
osei.misdirection: He'd add a large risk premium to Helix on top of the usual one, which double-counts.

lund.facts: Helix is the first project Halden has proposed outside oil and refining since the merger.
lund.stance: If Halden never starts something new, the board will decide what it becomes for it.
lund.signal: Ask them what each project says about the company they wrote down in their sentence.
lund.misdirection: She wants Helix even if the numbers say it adds less this quarter.

priya.facts: Marcus Delacroix wants the Baton Rouge upgrade. Bjørn Aasen wants the Rotterdam one. Margrethe Lund wants Helix. Ingrid Vestergaard has to take the choice to the board.
priya.stance: Predictions: whichever project loses, its champion will ask for a meeting within a week. If the team picks Baton Rouge, Marcus will be loyal for a quarter. If it picks Helix, Margrethe will mention it at the next board meeting. If it picks nothing, Ingrid will feel she wasted a quarter.
priya.misdirection: She thinks Bjørn will take a lost Rotterdam upgrade quietly. He won't.
